prompt: Which of the following statements about management control are correct?

options.text: It is a dynamic performance management (steering) process.
It is the sole responsibility of the management controller.
The management controller supports managers in designing and implementing the management system (business partner role).
The term "control" has a broad meaning here and is not limited to verification.

explanation: Management control is a dynamic performance steering process and the responsibility of managers. The controller supports them as a business partner – it is not the controller's sole remit.

prompt: The control cycle (performance management process) consists of which main phases?

options.text: A planning phase upstream of the action
A monitoring and analysis phase of the results downstream of the action
An external audit phase of the financial statements
A strategy formulation phase carried out by the board

explanation: The control cycle has two main phases: planning (before the action) and monitoring/analysis of results (after the action). Analysis can feed back into planning – hence the term "cycle".

prompt: Which are the fundamental qualities expected of measurements in a measurement system?

options.text: Validity with respect to the objective
Reliability
Ease of implementation
Exhaustiveness (covering every aspect of performance)
Being identical across all organisations

explanation: The three fundamental qualities are validity with respect to the objective, reliability and ease of implementation. In addition, measurement systems must respect the principle of relevance (adapted to their use).

prompt: The quality "ease of implementation" of a measurement includes …

options.text: the cost of producing the measurement
its timely delivery
its ease of interpretation
its ability to quantify a result with a limited margin of error

explanation: Ease of implementation = cost, timeliness and ease of interpretation. Quantifying a result with a limited margin of error is the definition of reliability.

prompt: At the level of an entity, which functions does the control cycle fulfil?

options.text: Regulation
Learning
External reporting to shareholders
Legal compliance of the statutory accounts

explanation: The control cycle fulfils two functions at entity level: regulation (updating action plans/targets based on results) and learning (updating the qualitative performance dimensions).

prompt: Which statements about measurement systems are correct?

options.text: Measurement systems are constructs.
One universal measurement system should serve all purposes in an organisation.
Their design varies depending on the purpose they are meant to serve (principle of relevance).
Relevant performance dimensions should first be made explicit in a qualitative way.
They may contain financial and/or non-financial dimensions.

explanation: Measurement systems are tailor-made constructs. Pursuing relevance implies that they are diverse, because each must be adapted to its intended use – there is no single universal system.

prompt: Which statements describe the principle of management by exception?

options.text: Only unfavourable gaps between objectives and results lead to special monitoring by managers.
Management should only intervene in an entity's operational decisions if its performance objectives are at risk.
Managers review every indicator in detail every period.
Favourable gaps automatically trigger a revision of the targets upwards.

explanation: Management by exception: only unfavourable gaps call for special attention; by extension, higher management only intervenes when the entity's objectives are at risk.

prompt: Regarding the granularity of performance management, which statements are correct?

options.text: One can look at the entity's overall performance (global view) or at sub-groups (analytical view).
Management accounting is useful for analysing performance by business segment.
Financial accounting is useful for breaking performance down by legal entity.
Financial accounting is the main tool for analysing performance by business segment.

explanation: Management accounting → analysis by business segment; financial accounting → breakdown by legal entity.

prompt: Which statements about management reporting and financial reporting are correct?

options.text: Management reporting informs managers about the performance of parts of the organisation for control purposes.
Consolidated financial statements mainly answer third-party (external) reporting purposes.
Financial accounting does not contribute to management reporting at all.
Financial reporting aggregates the individual financial statements of each legal entity.

explanation: Financial accounting also helps executives manage accounting and tax issues of their legal entities, so it contributes to management reporting – just more marginally.

prompt: Which statements about autonomous control are correct?

options.text: It is carried out locally by the managers in charge of responsibility centres.
It differs from the control exercised by managers at higher hierarchical levels.
It is designed to monitor the entity's own performance.
It is carried out by external auditors.

explanation: The management control process runs primarily within each responsibility centre as an autonomous control process led by local managers.

prompt: In which kinds of organisations is management control useful?

options.text: Large groups
SMEs (possibly in a simplified form)
Non-profit organisations with a wide range of performance objectives
Public institutions

explanation: Management control is neither limited to large nor to profit-seeking organisations; it is useful wherever performance objectives are pursued.

statement: Management control is only relevant for large organisations.
explanation: SMEs are also concerned, even if their management system is sometimes more simplified.

statement: The analysis of results can lead to feedback on planning, which is why the process is called a regulation "cycle".
explanation: Planning → action → monitoring/analysis → feedback to planning.

statement: Reliability is the ability of a measurement to accurately reflect the phenomenon being measured or the intention underlying the objective.
explanation: That is validity with respect to the objective. Reliability = quantifying a result with a limited margin of error.

statement: The learning loop is the process of updating the qualitative dimensions of performance that underlie the measurement system.
explanation: Learning updates the performance dimensions themselves; regulation updates action plans or targets.

statement: Regulation means taking the results obtained into account to update action plans or targets, with a view to improving performance.
explanation: This is the definition of regulation in the control cycle.

statement: The performance dimensions underlying a measurement system must always be financial.
explanation: Performance dimensions can be financial and/or non-financial; measurement systems are tailor-made.

statement: An indicator is a measure chosen to monitor the achievement of an objective; it allows the objective to be set and the result to be evaluated.
explanation: Definition of an indicator from Session 1a.

statement: The control cycle is based on measurement systems that structure both the planning phase and the monitoring and analysis phase.
explanation: Sets of indicators structure each of the two phases.

statement: Management reporting is mainly intended for users outside the organisation.
explanation: That describes external reporting. Management reporting informs managers for management control purposes.

prompt: Define management control.
modelAnswer: Management control is a process involving devices and practices that enable an organisation to set performance objectives and to effectively oversee their progressive achievement – in other words, a (dynamic) performance steering process. It is the responsibility of managers, supported by the management controller.
keyPoints: Process of devices and practices
Setting performance objectives
Overseeing their progressive achievement (performance steering)
Responsibility of managers (controller as support / business partner)

prompt: Explain the control cycle and the two functions it fulfils at the level of an entity.
modelAnswer: The control cycle is the dynamics of managing performance in two phases: planning (upstream of the action, setting objectives) and monitoring and analysis of results (downstream). Both phases are structured by measurement systems. Results feed back into planning. It fulfils two functions: regulation – using results to update action plans or targets – and learning – updating the qualitative performance dimensions underlying the measurement system (learning loop).
keyPoints: Planning phase (upstream of the action)
Monitoring and analysis of results (downstream)
Feedback of results into planning (cycle), based on measurement systems
Regulation: update action plans / targets
Learning: update the qualitative performance dimensions

prompt: State the three fundamental qualities expected of measurements and the additional principle measurement systems must adhere to.
modelAnswer: 1) Validity with respect to the objective – accurately reflecting the phenomenon/intention measured. 2) Reliability – quantifying a result with a limited margin of error. 3) Ease of implementation – cost, timely delivery, ease of interpretation. In addition, the principle of relevance: a measurement system must be adapted to its intended use.
keyPoints: Validity with respect to the objective
Reliability
Ease of implementation
Principle of relevance (adapted to intended use)

prompt: Which statements describe a responsibility centre?

options.text: An entity of the organisational structure placed under the authority of a manager
The group's leaders have delegated more or less decision-making power to its manager
Performance targets to be achieved have been set for its manager
It must always be a separate legal entity
It can be a department, a division or even the organisation itself

explanation: A responsibility centre is an organisational (not necessarily legal) unit under a manager with delegated decision power and performance targets – from a department up to the whole organisation.

prompt: Which statements about a business segment are correct?

options.text: It is a subdivision of an organisation's or a responsibility centre's overall activity, e.g. by product or type of market.
It can be evaluated with regard to management decisions such as developing or withdrawing from a business or allocating resources.
It is required to publish statutory financial statements.
Performance by business segment is mainly analysed with financial accounting.

explanation: Business segments are activity subdivisions relevant for management decisions; they are analysed with management accounting. Publishing statutory accounts is a feature of legal entities.

prompt: Which statements about a legal entity are correct?

options.text: It is a legal subdivision within a group.
It is required to publish statutory financial statements (company accounts).
Financial accounting is a useful measurement system for breaking performance down by legal entity.
It is defined as a subdivision of activity by product or market.

explanation: Legal entities publish company accounts; financial accounting breaks performance down by legal entity, whereas management accounting analyses business segments.

prompt: Which statements correctly link performance dimensions, objectives, indicators and measurement systems?

options.text: An objective is the operational translation of a performance dimension in the form of a type of result to be achieved.
An indicator is a measure chosen to monitor the achievement of an objective.
A measurement system is a set of indicators to assess performance for a given purpose.
Relevant performance dimensions are only defined after the indicators have been chosen.

explanation: The logic runs from qualitatively defined performance dimensions to objectives, then to indicators that are combined into measurement systems – not the other way round.

prompt: A sales indicator is calculated very precisely, but it does not capture the intention behind the objective of building long-term customer relationships. Which quality of the measurement is lacking?

options.text: Validity with respect to the objective
Reliability
Ease of implementation

explanation: Validity is the ability of a measurement to accurately reflect the phenomenon measured or the intention underlying the objective. Precision (limited margin of error) is reliability, which is given here.

prompt: A measure can only be estimated with a large margin of error. Which quality of the measurement is weak?

options.text: Reliability
Validity with respect to the objective
Ease of implementation

explanation: Reliability is the extent to which a measurement can quantify a result with a limited margin of error.

prompt: What does the principle of relevance imply for measurement systems?

options.text: A measurement can serve multiple uses.
A measurement must be adapted to the specific use for which it is intended.
Measurement systems are diverse; their design varies with their purpose.
One standard set of indicators should be used for every purpose to ensure comparability.

explanation: Relevance means aligning measurements with their intended use, which is why measurement systems are diverse and tailor-made.

prompt: Which statements about financial reporting and financial accounting are correct?

options.text: Financial reporting is often equated with external reporting.
Financial accounting enables executives to manage the accounting and tax issues of the legal entities under their responsibility.
Financial accounting contributes to management reporting, albeit in a more marginal way.
Financial accounting is the primary measurement system for analysing performance by business segment.

explanation: Consolidated statements serve third parties, so financial reporting is equated with external reporting, but it also marginally supports management reporting. Segment analysis relies on management accounting.

prompt: Which issues does management control raise specifically in large groups ("to go further")?

options.text: Vertical coordination and strategic alignment between the operational control of units and global performance management
Horizontal coordination between responsibility centres, e.g. internal transactions and transfer pricing
Orienting managers' behaviour, e.g. through results control or cultural control
Abolishing measurement systems because they demotivate managers

explanation: Large groups face vertical coordination, horizontal coordination (transfer pricing) and behavioural issues – measurement systems matter a lot for motivation and evaluation, but are not abolished.

prompt: After analysing a negative gap, a manager revises the action plan and the targets for the next period. Which function of the control cycle does this illustrate?

options.text: Regulation
Learning
External reporting

explanation: Regulation takes the results obtained into account to update action plans or targets. Learning would mean updating the qualitative performance dimensions behind the measurement system.

prompt: Management realises that customer loyalty, not just sales volume, is a key dimension of performance and redesigns its indicators accordingly. Which function of the control cycle does this illustrate?

options.text: Learning (learning loop)
Regulation
Management by exception

explanation: The learning loop updates the qualitative dimensions of performance underlying the measurement system.

statement: Transfer pricing and the monitoring of internal transactions are issues of horizontal coordination between responsibility centres.
explanation: Horizontal coordination between responsibility centres, including internal transactions and transfer pricing, is one of the most difficult issues in management control.

statement: Vertical coordination and strategic alignment concern how the operational control process of units is articulated with a more strategic and global performance management process.
explanation: This is the 'to go further' issue of vertical coordination in large groups.

statement: Measurement systems are standardised and can be transferred unchanged from one organisation to another.
explanation: Measurement systems are constructs built on the organisation's relevant performance dimensions – they are tailor-made for each organisation.

statement: A business segment is a legal subdivision of a group that must publish statutory financial statements.
explanation: That is a legal entity. A business segment is a subdivision of activity (product, market type …) relevant for management decisions.

statement: Under management by exception, favourable gaps between objectives and results are the main trigger for special monitoring by managers.
explanation: Only unfavourable gaps lead to special monitoring.

statement: Validity with respect to the objective is the extent to which a measurement can quantify a result with a limited margin of error.
explanation: That is reliability. Validity is the ability to accurately reflect the phenomenon measured or the intention underlying the objective.

statement: Relevance means that a measurement must be adapted to the specific use for which it is intended.
explanation: Because a measurement can serve multiple uses, it must be aligned with its intended use.

statement: Autonomous control is carried out by managers at higher hierarchical levels on behalf of the responsibility centres.
explanation: Autonomous control is carried out locally by the managers in charge of the responsibility centres; it differs from control by higher hierarchical levels.

statement: In management control, "control" means only checking compliance after the fact.
explanation: The term 'control' has a broad meaning: management control is a dynamic performance management (steering) process.

statement: Human stakes behind measurement systems are high in large groups because these systems play an important role in managers' motivation and evaluation.
explanation: That is why approaches to orient behaviour (results control, cultural control …) matter.

statement: The planning phase takes place downstream of the action, the monitoring phase upstream.
explanation: It is the other way round: planning is upstream of the action, monitoring and analysis of results downstream.

prompt: Define a responsibility centre.
modelAnswer: A responsibility centre is an entity of the organisational structure that the group's leaders have placed under the authority of a manager, to whom they have delegated more or less decision-making power and for whom they have set performance targets to be achieved (e.g. a department, a division or the organisation itself).
keyPoints: Entity of the organisational structure
Placed under the authority of a manager
Delegated (more or less) decision-making power
Performance targets set for the manager

prompt: Define the principle of management by exception.
modelAnswer: Management by exception is the principle that only unfavourable gaps between objectives and results achieved lead to special monitoring by managers. By extension, management should only intervene in an entity's operational decisions if the entity's performance objectives are at risk.
keyPoints: Only unfavourable gaps between objectives and results
Trigger special monitoring by managers
By extension: intervene only if performance objectives are at risk

prompt: Explain the difference between management reporting and external (financial) reporting.
modelAnswer: Management reporting is a measurement system that informs managers about the performance of parts of the organisation for management control purposes. External reporting is intended for users outside the organisation; financial reporting produces the consolidated financial statements of a group by aggregating the legal entities' statements and is therefore often equated with external reporting, although financial accounting also contributes marginally to management reporting.
keyPoints: Management reporting: informs managers about performance of parts of the organisation
Used for management control purposes (internal)
External reporting: for users outside the organisation
Financial reporting / consolidated statements mostly serve external purposes
Financial accounting contributes only marginally to management reporting

prompt: Explain the principle of relevance and what it implies for the design of measurement systems.
modelAnswer: A measurement or measurement system can serve multiple uses, so it must be adapted to the specific use for which it is intended. Pursuing relevance implies that measurement systems are diverse: their design varies with the purpose they serve, and they are tailor-made for each organisation based on its explicitly defined performance dimensions.
keyPoints: Measurements can serve multiple uses
Must be adapted/aligned to the intended use
Measurement systems are therefore diverse
Design varies with purpose / tailor-made for each organisation

prompt: State the definitions of validity with respect to the objective and of reliability.
modelAnswer: Validity with respect to the objective is the ability of a measurement to accurately reflect the phenomenon being measured or the intention underlying the objective pursued. Reliability is the extent to which a measurement can quantify a result with a limited margin of error.
keyPoints: Validity: accurately reflects the phenomenon measured / the intention behind the objective
Reliability: quantifies a result with a limited margin of error
